Thought for 11s

I've built the Pomodoro timer and checked every requirement, both with automated tests and by clicking through it in a real browser. Everything passed at both sizes, and the browser showed no errors.

It uses a calm sage and cream look. During breaks the colors shift to a soft blue, and on a phone the settings panel opens from the bottom of the screen. I've called it "Tomato" for now, so tell me if you'd like a different name.

What I tested and how:

Logic tests (12, all passing):
The 25/5/15 minute defaults.
The long break coming after every 4th focus session, with the order checked over 8 phases.
Skipping a focus session doesn't count toward the long break.
Remaining time is worked out from clock time, so it stays correct after a 10-minute gap with no updates.
Pausing and resuming keeps the right time.
Reset puts the full time back.
The countdown and tab title read like "12:04 - Focus".
Durations must be whole numbers from 1 to 90; 0, 91, blank, letters and decimals are all rejected.
Damaged saved settings fall back to the defaults.
Today's log drops sessions from yesterday.
Browser check at 1280px and 375px wide: I used a simulated clock so I could jump minutes ahead instantly.
The space bar starts the timer. After 65 seconds the countdown and tab title both showed "23:55 - Focus".
Space paused it, and the time stayed frozen for 30 seconds.
Reset brought back 25:00, and Skip moved to the short break.
In settings, entering 91 showed an error and kept Save greyed out.
I set the durations to 1, 1 and 2 minutes and turned the sound off.
I ran 4 focus sessions, each with its own task label. The dots went from 1 of 4 up to 4 of 4, and the long break started after the 4th.
After reloading the page, all 4 log entries (labels and finish times), the new durations and the sound setting were still there.
I looked at screenshots of both sizes to check the layout.

Not checked: I didn't listen for the end-of-phase sound, since the test browser has no audio. I also didn't test a real background tab; I tested the clock-time logic it relies on instead.
